little-ice-age.name: Little Ice Age
little-ice-age.summary: A period of regional cooling, mainly in the North Atlantic, usually dated from the 16th to 19th centuries or as early as 1300, with proposed causes including solar and volcanic activity.

bergen.name: Bergen
bergen.summary: Norway's second-largest city, on the west coast, founded by tradition in 1070 and later a major Hanseatic League trading centre.

trondheim.name: Trondheim
trondheim.summary: A city in Norway founded in 997 that served as the country's capital through the Viking Age until 1217, and later became the seat of the Archdiocese of Nidaros.

dorset-culture.name: Dorset culture
dorset-culture.summary: A Paleo-Eskimo culture in the North American Arctic, lasting from about 500 BCE until it died out by 1000–1500 CE, before the Thule (proto-Inuit) arrived. Inuit legends recall its people as the Tuniit.

medieval-warm-period.name: Medieval Warm Period
medieval-warm-period.summary: A period of warm climate in the North Atlantic region lasting from about 950 to 1250 CE, not uniform worldwide and followed by the cooler Little Ice Age.

norton-tradition.name: Norton tradition
norton-tradition.summary: An archaeological culture along Alaska's Bering Strait coast from about 1000 BC to 800 AD, whose people hunted caribou and sea mammals and used new technologies like oil lamps and pottery.

st-lawrence-island.name: St. Lawrence Island
st-lawrence-island.summary: An island in the Bering Sea between Alaska and Russia, thought to be one of the last exposed remnants of the ancient land bridge joining Asia and North America.

thule-people.name: Thule people
thule-people.summary: The precursors of modern Inuit and Yupik peoples, who developed in coastal Alaska by 1000 CE, spread across the Arctic, and replaced the earlier Dorset culture by the 15th century.

saga-of-the-greenlanders.name: Saga of the Greenlanders
saga-of-the-greenlanders.summary: One of two main Icelandic sources on the Norse colonization of North America, describing events around 1000 CE, including six expeditions from Greenland led by figures such as Leif Erikson and Freydís Eiríksdóttir.

qulliq.name: Qulliq
qulliq.summary: A traditional oil lamp used by circumpolar peoples including the Inuit, fueled by seal oil or blubber and made of soapstone; a vital source of Arctic warmth and light.

erik-the-red.name: Erik the Red
erik-the-red.summary: Norse explorer (c. 950–c. 1003) credited with founding the first European settlement in Greenland after being exiled from Iceland around 982.

hvalsey.name: Hvalsey
hvalsey.summary: Site of Greenland's largest, best-preserved Norse ruins, part of the Eastern Settlement and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

gwyn-jones-author.name: Gwyn Jones
gwyn-jones-author.summary: Welsh novelist (1907–1999) and scholar and translator of Nordic literature and history.

cape-farewell-greenland.name: Cape Farewell
cape-farewell-greenland.summary: The southernmost point of Greenland, a headland on Egger Island regarded as one of the country's important landmarks.

saga-of-erik-the-red.name: Saga of Erik the Red
saga-of-erik-the-red.summary: A 13th-century Icelandic saga on Norse exploration of North America, mainly chronicling the expedition of Thorfinn Karlsefni and Gudrid, including Erik the Red's exile to Greenland and Leif Erikson's discovery of Vinland.

vinland.name: Vinland
vinland.summary: Area of coastal North America explored by Vikings, where Leif Erikson landed around AD 1000, long before Columbus; Norse building remains confirming it were found at L'Anse aux Meadows, Newfoundland, in 1960.

greenlandic-norse.name: Greenlandic Norse
greenlandic-norse.summary: An extinct North Germanic language spoken in Norse Greenland until the settlements' demise in the late 15th century, known mainly from runic inscriptions and believed to have been in contact with the Greenlandic language.

kingittorsuaq-runestone.name: Kingittorsuaq Runestone
kingittorsuaq-runestone.summary: A runestone found on Kingittorsuaq Island in northwestern Greenland, bearing one of the longest known Norse inscriptions in Greenland, traditionally dated to around 1300.

upernavik.name: Upernavik
upernavik.summary: A small town on an island in northwestern Greenland, with about 1,087 inhabitants as of 2025.

gar-ar-greenland.name: Garðar
gar-ar-greenland.summary: The seat of the bishop in Norse Greenland, and the first Catholic diocese established anywhere in the Americas.

atlam-l.name: Atlamál
atlam-l.summary: Heroic poem of the Poetic Edda likely composed in Greenland in the 12th century, retelling the story of Atlakviða at greater length in the málaháttr metre.

codex-regius.name: Codex Regius
codex-regius.summary: An Icelandic manuscript from the 1270s that is the main source for most poems of the Poetic Edda, later sent to Denmark and returned to Iceland in 1971.

var-b-r-arson.name: Ívar Bárðarson
var-b-r-arson.summary: A 14th-century Norwegian clergyman who served as the Catholic Church's official representative in Greenland; his reports are among the few primary sources on medieval Norse Greenland.

bj-rn-j-nsson-skar-s.name: Björn Jónsson á Skarðsá
bj-rn-j-nsson-skar-s.summary: A 17th-century Icelandic farmer and member of the Icelandic Court of Legislature, best known as author of the chronicle Skarðsárannáll, covering 1400 to his own day.

markland.name: Markland
markland.summary: One of three lands on North America's Atlantic coast, south of Helluland and north of Vinland, discovered by Leif Eriksson around 1000 AD; likely visited later for timber though never settled.

helge-ingstad.name: Helge Ingstad
helge-ingstad.summary: A Norwegian explorer (1899–2001) who, with his wife Anne Stine Ingstad, discovered a Viking settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland in 1960, proving Norse crossings to North America centuries before Columbus.

anne-stine-ingstad.name: Anne Stine Ingstad
anne-stine-ingstad.summary: Norwegian archaeologist who, with her husband Helge Ingstad, discovered the remains of a Norse settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in 1960, proving Norse voyages to North America centuries before Columbus.

l-anse-aux-meadows.name: L'Anse aux Meadows
l-anse-aux-meadows.summary: A Norse settlement site on Newfoundland's northern tip, dated to around 1000 CE by carbon and tree-ring evidence, the only confirmed pre-Columbian European site in the Americas outside Greenland.

ludvig-holberg.name: Ludvig Holberg
ludvig-holberg.summary: Norwegian-born writer, philosopher and playwright (1684–1754), considered the founder of modern Danish and Norwegian literature, best known for comedies written in the 1720s.

narsarsuaq.name: Narsarsuaq
narsarsuaq.summary: A small settlement in southern Greenland whose economy long depended on Narsarsuaq Airport, a former U.S. military base, alongside a tourism trade in wildlife, gemstones and glaciers.

western-settlement.name: Western Settlement
western-settlement.summary: A Norse farming community in medieval Greenland founded around 985, smaller than its companion Eastern Settlement and found abandoned when last visited in the 14th century.

cambridge-bay.name: Cambridge Bay
cambridge-bay.summary: A hamlet on Victoria Island in Canada's Arctic, named for the Duke of Cambridge; today it's the largest stop for ships crossing the Northwest Passage.

kalmar-union.name: Kalmar Union
kalmar-union.summary: A personal union joining Denmark, Sweden and Norway (with Norway's colonies) under one monarch from 1397 to 1523, agreed at Kalmar and designed by Queen Margaret of Denmark.

eastern-settlement.name: Eastern Settlement
eastern-settlement.summary: The larger of two main Norse colonies in Greenland, settled around 985 to 1000 CE from Iceland and home to about 4,000 people at its peak, with its last written record dated 1408.

denmark-norway.name: Denmark-Norway
denmark-norway.summary: A real union of the kingdoms of Denmark and Norway (with Norway's overseas possessions) plus Schleswig and Holstein, lasting from the 16th to 19th centuries.

nidaros.name: Nidaros
nidaros.summary: Medieval name for Trondheim, capital of Norway's first Christian kings and home to the shrine of Saint Olaf, a major pilgrimage site.

sigurd-the-crusader.name: Sigurd the Crusader
sigurd-the-crusader.summary: King of Norway from 1103 to 1130, known as the Crusader King as one of three co-regents who took part in the Norwegian Crusade of 1107–1110, regarded as the first king to take part in a crusade.

magnus-eriksson.name: Magnus Eriksson
magnus-eriksson.summary: King of Sweden from 1319 to 1364 and King of Norway (as Magnus VII) from 1319 to 1355; his long reign brought major legal reforms, including Sweden's first countrywide law code.

haakon-vi.name: Haakon VI
haakon-vi.summary: King of Norway from 1343 until his death in 1380, and King of Sweden from 1362 to 1364, ruling Sweden jointly with his father Magnus.

angakkuq.name: Angakkuq
angakkuq.summary: A spiritual and intellectual figure in Inuit culture who serves a role similar to a medicine man or shaman, with comparable figures found among other Alaska Native peoples.

inughuit.name: Inughuit
inughuit.summary: An ethnic subgroup of Greenlandic Inuit, the northernmost group of Inuit and people in North America, making up about 1% of Greenland's population.

sedna-mythology.name: Sedna
sedna-mythology.summary: The Inuit goddess of the sea and marine animals, also called Mother of the Sea, said to rule over the underworld Adlivun.

adlivun.name: Adlivun
adlivun.summary: In Inuit religion, the underworld beneath the land and sea where the spirits of the dead are purified before moving on to their final resting place, ruled over by the goddess Sedna.

toggling-harpoon.name: Toggling harpoon
toggling-harpoon.summary: An ancient whaling weapon whose two-part point detaches and twists under the animal's skin when thrust in, preventing it from slipping out.

saint-nicholas.name: Saint Nicholas
saint-nicholas.summary: Early Christian bishop of Greek descent from Patara in Anatolia (c. 270 to 343), patron saint of sailors among others, whose legendary gift-giving inspired the folklore of Santa Claus.

diocese-of-lund.name: Diocese of Lund
diocese-of-lund.summary: A diocese established in 1060 that, from 1104, held authority over church affairs across Denmark, Norway and Sweden as the Archdiocese of Lund.

roman-catholic-archdiocese-of-nidaros.name: Archdiocese of Nidaros
roman-catholic-archdiocese-of-nidaros.summary: Metropolitan church district covering Norway from the mid-12th century until the Reformation, seated at Nidaros Cathedral in what is now Trondheim.

kinngait.name: Kinngait
kinngait.summary: An Inuit hamlet on Dorset Island near Baffin Island in Nunavut, Canada, known as Cape Dorset until 2020.

nunavut.name: Nunavut
nunavut.summary: Canada's largest and northernmost territory, created in 1999 from the Northwest Territories to provide the Inuit with self-government.

qilakitsoq.name: Qilakitsoq
qilakitsoq.summary: An abandoned settlement in Greenland where eight mummified Inuit bodies from the Thule period, about 500 years old, were discovered.

pope-innocent-iii.name: Pope Innocent III
pope-innocent-iii.summary: One of the most powerful medieval popes, ruling the Catholic Church and Papal States from 1198 to 1216, who greatly expanded the Crusades and reformed canon law.
